materials.title: 图书馆规则与请求：can、there be、this / these 与位置
materials.instructions: 先看图书馆情境中的规则和例句，再独立完成 14 题。提交后查看正确表达与原因。
materials.passage:
1. 说明能力或允许的行为，用 can + 动词原形：You can renew the book. You cannot take reference books home. cannot / can't 表示不允许或不能；can 后不加 to，也不使用第三人称 -s。

2. 请求许可用 Can I + 原形：Can I use this computer, please? 请求别人帮助用 Can you + 原形：Can you help me find the science section? 问句只把 can 放到主语前，不再加 do。

3. 表示某处有某物：There is a dictionary on the table. There are two computers near the desk. 单数用 is，复数用 are。一般疑问句为 Is there a printer? / Are there any novels? 注意 there 不表示“他们”。

4. 近处单数 this book，近处复数 these books；远处单数 that shelf，远处复数 those shelves。This book is available. These books are available. shelf 的复数是 shelves，不是 shelfs。

5. 位置介词：on the shelf 在架子上；in the science section 在科学类区域；beside the window 在窗旁；at the back 在后部。它们表达不同空间关系，不能只按一个中文“在”来选。

6. 指令用动词原形：Read the description first. Keep quiet. 否定用 Don't + 原形：Don't talk near the study desks. can 后也要原形：You can search by title. 先读规则，再用这些句型写自己的借书说明。

materials.title: Finding Useful Information at the Library
materials.passage:
Maya and Leo visit the local library on Tuesday afternoon. They want to find information for a short talk about animals. A librarian welcomes them and explains how to use the building. Each visitor needs a library card to take a book home. A normal loan lasts two weeks. Visitors can renew a book once if nobody else needs it, but they must ask before the return date.

The librarian shows them a computer near the desk. Its screen displays a list of books. They can search by author, title or topic. Maya types the name of an animal and sees twelve results. She does not select the first result immediately. She checks whether each book is available and reads a short description. One useful book is already with another reader. Maya can reserve it and collect it when it comes back.

Leo walks along the wide aisle to the fiction section. He finds a short novel with a green cover. Its author also writes stories for younger readers. Leo opens the first chapter and reads one page to check the difficulty. He enjoys the story, but it does not answer their questions about real animals. They decide to read it at home later rather than use it for the talk.

For their project, they need a different resource. The librarian recommends an information book on the top shelf. An index at the back lists important words and the pages where they appear. This helps the learners find facts without reading every chapter. There is also a dictionary on the reference table. It explains unfamiliar words. Reference books stay inside the building so that everyone can use them.

The reading area is quiet. A sign asks for silence near the study desks, while conversations are allowed in a separate room. Maya and Leo take notes there and compare the facts they have found. A printer beside the computers can produce a copy of their notes for ten cents per page. They print only two pages. Before leaving, they check the book's return date and put the dictionary back. They now have enough information to prepare their talk together.

materials.title: Club Plans: Questions, Reasons and Requests
materials.passage:
今天把俱乐部活动用于问时间、说明习惯与提出请求。

1. 用 be 问状态：Are you free? Yes, I am. 用 do 问动作或喜好：Do you like math? Yes, I do. 问时间可用 When are you free? I am free on Wednesday morning. 问最喜欢的学科：What is your favorite subject? My favorite subject is math.

2. 一般现在时中，第三人称单数常在动词后加 s：Nora works at a clinic. 复数主语用复数形式：The people are ready.

3. 位置：in Room 5 表示在5号房间；on the desk 表示在桌面上；next to the clock 表示在钟旁边。

4. because 引出原因：I bring a pen because I want to write. can 后接动词原形：Can you turn on the lamp, please?

5. 真实未来条件可以用 if + 一般现在时，主句可用 will + 原形：If I am busy, I will send a message. 提建议也可用祈使句：If you need more light, turn on the lamp.

6. 直接问地点是 Where is the room? 嵌入礼貌请求后用陈述语序：Can you tell me where the room is, please?

materials.instructions: Read the whole passage. Choose ONE answer for each multiple-choice question. For short answers, use words from the passage and follow the word limit.
materials.passage:
On Monday morning, Maya and Leo walk to the English club at their language school. Outside Room 5, Maya can see a woman named Nora. Nora is Leo's neighbor and a doctor. She wants to learn English so she can speak to visitors at work.

In the hallway, Maya points to a white folder on a table. A lamp lights the table. Leo places a yellow notebook on a brown chair. He carries a long ruler and a cup in his bag.

Inside, Ms. Chen welcomes the three people: Maya, Leo, and Nora. It is Nora's first club meeting, and she is a new member. Leo says, "We are on the same team today." Their task is to make a short welcome poster for other students.

During a break, Nora asks, "What is your favorite subject, Leo?" "Math," he says, "but I also enjoy learning English." Maya writes their names on a white card and puts it next to the clock.

At the end of the meeting, Ms. Chen asks the team to choose a time to practice again. Nora is busy on Tuesday because she works at a clinic, but she is free on Wednesday morning. Maya and Leo are free then, too, so they agree to meet here.

Before leaving, Nora stops to say, "Good luck with your class, Maya." Maya thanks her. She likes the club because the members listen to one another.

When they meet again on Wednesday, Ms. Chen places three blue practice cards in a box. Each card has a different opening question. She asks the members to practice with a partner before choosing another card. Nora practices with Maya. Meanwhile, Leo listens and writes down words for the group to review. The members keep the questions short because visitors will have only a few minutes. At the end, Leo puts the cards on a shelf beside the door.

Before leaving, Maya writes a schedule for Wednesday. The first activity is a short conversation with a visitor. Ten minutes of practice will help each member prepare. Maya sends a message with the meeting place and asks everyone to reply by Tuesday. Anyone who cannot attend can choose another time instead of missing the conversation completely.

materials.title: 数量与步骤：there is / are、some / any 与先后顺序
materials.instructions: 先读规则，再独立完成 14 题。注意可数名词、不可数名词和制作步骤之间的先后关系。
materials.passage:
本课把基础句型推进到“有什么、需要多少、先做什么”。

1. there is + 单数名词或不可数名词：There is a brush. There is some paint. there are + 复数名词：There are four brushes. 这是说明某处有什么，不是说它们在做什么。

2. brush、shape 和 tool 可数，复数用 brushes、shapes、tools。本课的 paper（纸）和 paint（颜料）通常不可数：some paper、some paint。数量用 a piece of paper / two pieces of paper；paint 的数量可用 a small amount of paint。不要把 brush 的 -es 规则误用于 paper。

3. 肯定句常用 some：There is some blue paint. 一般问句和否定句常用 any：Is there any red paint? There isn't any red paint. 提供或礼貌索取、期待肯定答复时也可以在问句中用 some：Can I have some paper, please?

4. How many + 复数可数名词：How many brushes are there? How much + 不可数名词：How much paint do we need? 回答具体数量前，先确认问题问的是人数、工具数量还是材料用量。

5. a/an 根据紧接其后的读音选择：a brush；an instruction（以元音读音开头）。形容词通常放在名词前：a careful learner。表达“要小心”用 Be careful；请求动作使用原形：Please return the ruler.

6. before / after 后可接完整从句：Read the instruction before you start. After the paint is dry, move the picture. while 表示同时：While we wait, we can put the tools away. 不可把 before（之前）、after（之后）与 while（期间）混淆。

materials.title: Sharing Tools and Checking the Steps
materials.transcript:
Maya: We have an hour for the welcome picture. Shall we start with the paint?
Leo: First, let's check the design. There is a sketch on the table, but I think the circle is too big.
Maya: You're right. We can make its size smaller and put it in the middle. The triangle can go at the top.
Leo: How many brushes are there for our group?
Maya: Two, and there are four of us. We can share them. You and I can paint while Nora and Sam cut the paper.
Leo: Is there any red paint?
Maya: No, there isn't. There is some blue paint. Let's use that for the circle.
Leo: All right. Can I borrow this ruler? I need to check the space near the edge.
Maya: Yes, but please return it to the next table by eleven. They need it for another project.
Leo: I made a small mistake in the bottom corner. Do I need to start again?
Maya: No. You can cover it with a spare piece of paper. Be careful when you attach it because the surface is still wet.
Leo: Then we should wait before moving the picture.
Maya: Exactly. The instruction says to wait twenty minutes for the paint to become dry. While we wait, let's put every tool back in its box.
Leo: Good idea. After that, we can explain our pattern to the other group.
materials.instructions: Listen to Maya and Leo. Choose ONE answer for each question. You can replay the audio; viewing the transcript is recorded as help.

materials.title: A Shared Studio Project
materials.passage:
On Wednesday, Maya and Leo join four other learners in a school art studio. Their project is a welcome picture for a community room. They have ninety minutes. Before they start, Mr. Lee shows them a simple design. Maya makes a quick sketch on old paper first. This lets the group change an idea before using expensive paper.

There are four brushes for six people, so they cannot all paint at once. Each brush is clean and ready. There is some blue and green paint, but there is no red paint. Paper is the main material for the project. A ruler is another useful tool. Each instruction on the wall describes one step. Mr. Lee asks the learners to read the steps before touching anything.

The group chooses a pattern with three different shapes. A circle goes in the middle. A square goes near the top, and a triangle goes at the bottom. Each shape has a different size. Maya checks one small detail: there must be space around every shape. She leaves two centimeters between the picture and the edge of the paper. Leo cleans the table because they need a smooth surface to work on.

The learners arrange the shapes before adding paint. They do not attach them immediately, because they may want to move them. Maya asks to borrow a ruler from the next table. She promises to return it before the lesson ends. The group decides to share the brushes: three people work while the others prepare paper. After fifteen minutes, they change jobs. Everyone must be careful with the wet picture. A small mistake can be corrected with a spare piece of paper, so nobody needs to start again.

At ten twenty, the picture is finished, but the paint is not dry. Mr. Lee explains that they must wait before putting it on the wall. While they wait, the group puts the tools away and checks the floor for drops of paint. At ten forty, the picture is ready to move. Leo takes it to the community room with Maya. They show the other learners what they made and explain which step was the most difficult. The group agrees that sharing tools and checking each step helped them finish on time.

materials.title: 讲述过去：was / were、过去式与 did 问句
materials.instructions: 先理解本课新结构，再独立作答。提交后查看原句、正确表达和原因。
materials.passage:
本课从“平时做什么”推进到“昨天发生了什么”。使用公园活动的词汇描述已结束的经历。

1. 过去的状态用 was / were：Yesterday, Ella was sad. The visitors were happy. I/he/she/it 常用 was；you/we/they 用 were。否定为 wasn't / weren't。不能把 Yesterday 和表示当前状态的 is 混用。

2. 已结束的动作使用过去式：Yesterday, we walked to the park. The worker helped us. They danced at the event. 规则动词通常加 -ed；以不发音的 e 结尾加 -d（dance → danced）。辅音字母加 y 常变 y 为 i 再加 -ed（carry → carried）。

3. 常用不规则形式：go → went，see → saw，give → gave，fall → fell，take → took。例：The sign fell down. We went to the park. Maya saw a volunteer. 不要把 went 再加 -ed。

4. 动作问句用 Did + 主语 + 动词原形：Did you walk to the park? Yes, I did. / No, I didn't. 否定用 didn't + 原形：Ben didn't swim in the lake. did 已表示过去，后面不再写 walked 或 swam。

5. 状态问句直接把 was / were 前移：Was Ella sad? Were the visitors happy? 不写 Did Ella was sad? 提问过去的活动可说 What did you do yesterday?

6. 连接事情先后：First, we fixed the sign. Then we watched the music event. Finally, we collected the badges. 对照习惯：We usually walk to the park, but yesterday we took the bus.

materials.title: A Weekend Event at the Park
materials.instructions: Read the whole passage. Choose ONE answer for each multiple-choice question. For short answers, use words from the passage and follow the word limit.
materials.passage:
On Saturday, Maya and Leo walk to the city park for a weekend event. At the gate, a young girl says, "Hi!" Her name is Ella. Ben, a boy of ten, waves too. Their grandfather, Mr. Hall, is an old man who lives nearby.

"I live near the park, and I work as a bus driver," Mr. Hall says. "My job starts early, so I enjoy a quiet morning here."

Ella feels sad because the paper sign for the music event has fallen down. A nice park worker brings tape and paper. Maya says, "We can make a new sign together."

"I like music," says Ella. "Can we sing and dance during the event?" The worker says yes, but asks the children not to swim in the cold lake. The path near the gate is safe for walking.

Ben wants to play football, called soccer in the United States, but he will watch a performance first. Families travel from other neighborhoods for the event. After hanging up the sign, the friends talk and laugh. They are a little tired, but they are happy to help.

Later, the worker opens a box of blank paper badges at the information table. Each visitor can write a first name on a badge; this lets volunteers welcome people without guessing. Ella offers to place pencils on the table. The worker asks Ben to put a small information sign for this table beside the box; it is separate from the music-event sign. The information sign tells visitors to return the pencils after writing. One pencil rolls under the table, so Maya picks it up and puts it in a cup. Near the end of the event, the worker collects the unused badges in an envelope and saves them for the next event.

On Sunday, Ella writes about the event in her diary. Yesterday, she was sad at first, but a volunteer helped her. The volunteer was Maya. The friends walked to the park, fixed the sign, and watched the performance. They did not swim because the lake was cold. Ella asks Ben, "Did you enjoy the event?" He says, "Yes, I did. I gave three visitors a badge and showed them the information table." Ella decides to write both the problem and the solution in her diary so she can explain the event clearly next week.

materials.title: 物品归属：宾格、物主代词与 whose
materials.instructions: 先理解本课新结构，再独立作答。提交后查看原句、正确表达和原因。
materials.passage:
本课围绕失物招领，说明“东西是谁的”和“交给谁”。

1. 动词或介词后用宾格：I → me，he → him，she → her，we → us，they → them。Please help me. Give the key to her. The worker asks them to wait. 主格 she 放在动作前，宾格 her 放在 to 后。

2. 形容词性物主代词后接名词：my phone、your key、her umbrella、our office、their camera。名词性物主代词独立使用：mine、yours、hers、ours、theirs。This phone is mine. This is my phone. 不能写 mine phone，也不能把 This phone is my. 当完整表达。

3. 询问归属用 Whose：Whose umbrella is this? It is hers. Whose keys are these? They are his. who 问人是谁，whose 问东西属于谁。

4. 人名加 's 表示所属：Maya's bag。单数 owner 的所属为 the owner's phone；规则复数 owners 的所属为 the owners' bags。it's 是 it is / it has 的缩写；its 表所属：The dog has its own bowl.

5. 用 it 指前文单数物品，用 them 指复数物品：I found a key. Please keep it. I found two keys. Please keep them. 不要因为物品没有生命就一律用 it。

6. 物品归属不确定时先问再推断：Is this jacket yours? No, mine is green. 描述所需动作继续使用 need to + 原形：We need to call the owner.

materials.title: A Visit to the Shelter Office
materials.instructions: Read the whole passage. Choose ONE answer for each multiple-choice question. For short answers, use words from the passage and follow the word limit.
materials.passage:
On Sunday, Maya and Leo take the bus to an animal shelter office. A map tells them to turn left at the library. At the door, a green sign shows the office entrance.

Outside, a dog plays with a ball. A cat waits in a separate room. A worker explains that each animal needs care before it can become a pet in a new home.

Near the office door they find a bag. Maya gives it to the worker. The worker checks the bag and records a phone, a key, a hat and an umbrella. The worker will keep the bag until its owner returns. She keeps the bag behind the counter so its owner has one clear place to ask.

Maya wears a jacket, and Leo carries a coat because the weather may change. A visitor brings a gift of clean towels. The worker asks Maya, "Please bring a bottle of water for the table."

Leo has an old photo of a mountain on his camera. He can use the camera to look at that photo. Maya first asks whether they may photograph the notice, and the worker agrees. The notice shows the office opening hours for volunteers. The worker puts a glass of water on the table for each visitor. Maya says, "I need a bus ticket for the journey home," and she has enough money. Before the office closes at four, the worker checks her list. She marks today’s date on its back so she can find the latest version. The list stays in the office rather than online so private details are not shared publicly. The friends plan to return on Wednesday to help sort towels. Before leaving, they thank the worker for her help.

A woman comes to the counter before closing. "Is this jacket yours?" the worker asks, pointing to a spare jacket. "No, mine is blue," the woman replies. She describes her missing bag and the things inside it before the worker shows them to her. Her description matches the record, so the worker returns the bag. Maya asks why the worker did not show every item first. The worker explains that asking for a description helps check who really owns the bag. The friends learn to ask whose things they are before giving them away.

Inside the bag, the worker finds a wallet in a small pocket. She does not show the money to the visitors. Instead, she uses the card inside to contact the owner privately. The owner describes the wallet before collecting the bag. This protects the belongings and helps the worker return them to the right person.

materials.title: 比较与用量：比较级、too much / many、enough
materials.instructions: 先理解本课新结构，再独立作答。提交后查看原句、正确表达和原因。
materials.passage:
本课用做饭的场景比较选择，并说明数量是否合适。上一课的物品归属继续用于描述厨房物品。

1. 常见短形容词比较级加 -er：fresh → fresher；bright → brighter。This apple is fresher than that one. big → bigger（双写末尾辅音）；形容词以 y 结尾时常变 y 为 i：easy → easier。

2. 较长形容词常用 more + 形容词：This recipe is more difficult than that one. 不写 more easier。比较对象后用 than，不是 then。good 的比较级是不规则的 better：This recipe is better for our group.

3. 从三个或更多对象中比较最高程度，常用 the + 最高级：This is the brightest room in the apartment. This is the easiest recipe of the three. 比较级与最高级需看语境，不要只靠一个关键词判断。

4. 数量太多：too many + 复数可数名词（too many eggs）；too much + 不可数名词（too much rice）。表示有一些用 a few + 可数复数（a few apples）或 a little + 不可数（a little tea）。

5. enough 放在名词前：enough food；放在形容词后：big enough。This bowl is big enough for the salad. There is enough rice for three people. too + 形容词表示超出合适程度：The coffee is too hot to drink.

6. 选择与偏好：I prefer tea to coffee. Would you like some tea? 提供饮品时可用 some，期待对方接受；不是所有问句都必须用 any。

materials.title: Planning a Shared Meal
materials.instructions: Read the whole passage. Choose ONE answer for each multiple-choice question. For short answers, use words from the passage and follow the word limit.
materials.passage:
On Tuesday, Maya and Leo visit Ms. Chen's apartment for a cooking class. Ms. Chen lived in Britain before. She explains that a flat is an apartment and a lift is an elevator. A cooker is often called a stove in the United States.

On the balcony, a small plant gets fresh air. The kitchen is bright, and an empty bowl is on the table. Ms. Chen puts bread on a plate and an apple beside it. She keeps a clean towel near the sink.

The friends plan a shared meal. Maya wants rice and chicken. Leo asks for a vegetable pie. Ms. Chen will eat fish today, but she does not want chicken. They check a recipe before they cook food together.

"We can buy fruit and an egg at the market," Maya says. "Would you like to drink tea or coffee after the meal?" Leo chooses tea, while Ms. Chen prefers coffee. The friends make a shopping list so they can prepare what each person wants.

Before shopping, Ms. Chen asks each person about the food they prefer and writes the answers on separate cards, so nobody is forgotten. The shop closes at six, so Maya and Leo plan to shop together before then. Ms. Chen will stay home and prepare the table. They will label the dishes so visitors can choose what suits them.

They compare two recipes before leaving. The vegetable pie has fewer steps than the other recipe, but it needs a bigger dish. Ms. Chen finds a bowl that is large enough to mix the filling. Leo suggests six eggs, but Maya says that is too many for this recipe: it needs only two. They already have enough rice and a little tea, so those items stay off the shopping list. materials.title: 出行计划：be going to、must / must not 与路线顺序
materials.instructions: 先理解本课新结构，再独立作答。提交后查看原句、正确表达和原因。
materials.passage:
本课把地点和方向词用于完整出行计划。复习第5课问句、第7课过去经历，以及第9课路线之间的比较。

1. 已经决定的计划可以用 be going to + 动词原形：We are going to visit the museum. She is going to take the bus. 主语变化时改变 am/is/are；going to 后不使用 visits。

2. 计划问句：Are you going to walk? Where are you going to meet? 否定：We are not going to drive. 过去实际发生的动作仍用过去式：Yesterday, we took the train.

3. must + 动词原形表达必须：You must cross at the signal. must not 表示禁止：You must not cross while the light is red. don't have to 表示不必：You don't have to buy a ticket because the talk is free. “禁止买”与“不必买”不同。

4. 路线指令用原形：Walk straight, then turn right. Go past the bakery. The museum is between the bakery and the restaurant. past 表示经过，across 表示从一边到另一边：Cross the street at the signal.

5. 顺序和终点：Before you cross, check the signal. After you cross, turn right. Walk until you reach the market. until 表示持续走到到达市场为止。

6. 礼貌询问：Could you tell me where the entrance is? 嵌入问句用陈述语序 entrance is，不写 where is the entrance。选择路线时给理由：We are going to take the shorter route because we have little time.

materials.title: Finding the Way in Town
materials.instructions: Read the whole passage. Choose ONE answer for each multiple-choice question. For short answers, use words from the passage and follow the word limit.
materials.passage:
On Monday, Maya and Leo visit a small town. At the station, Leo checks a paper map of the town. The train station has a long hall that leads to the ticket office, and a bus stop is in front of the station. A sign on the left points toward the stairs. A bench near the station gives people a place to rest.

"Excuse me, where is the museum?" Maya asks. A worker says, "The museum is between the bakery and the restaurant." She adds, "Walk straight along this street. Cross the street at the signal. Turn right at the corner and walk to the market. The museum is just past the market." A small shop is next to the market. The supermarket is not far from the clinic. The hospital is across the park. People can ask a worker for help, and the worker can answer their questions.

In the afternoon, a free local art talk starts at three. Maya would like to go, but Leo must send an email first. The worker writes the room number on a blue card. The friends decide to return to the desk at two forty-five so they will not miss the start. Before they leave the station, they read the route together. "If another question comes up, please come back to this desk," the worker says. Maya thanks her for the help.

Maya checks the direction of the museum entrance on the map. The short route goes past the market, while a longer route passes through the park. They are going to take the shorter one because they want to return before the art talk. At the crossing, the light is red. Leo says they must not cross yet. They wait until it changes, then continue toward the museum. They do not have to buy a ticket for the art talk, but they still need to arrive on time. Maya writes the meeting point and the return time in her notebook before putting the map away.

materials.title: 正在发生、日常习惯与已安排的行程
materials.instructions: 先比较三个时间含义，再独立选答；订正时说清主语、时间线索和动词形式。
materials.passage:
1. 正在发生：am / is / are + 动词-ing。Owen is pulling a suitcase. Jade is checking the display. 主语复数用 are：They are waiting on the platform. 否定把 not 放在 be 后：They are not boarding yet. 问句把 be 提到主语前：Are they waiting here? 不再添加 do。

2. 日常习惯用一般现在时：The commuter travels every weekday. I travel on Mondays. 第三人称单数加 -s；today / now 发生的临时活动常用现在进行时：Today she is visiting her sister. 注意判断句意，不能仅凭一个时间词套公式。

3. 已确定的未来安排也可用现在进行时：Our friend is meeting us at the station tomorrow. 这里不是说她此刻已在见我们，而是双方约好的安排。与前课 going to 表示意图相联系；本课区分安排与眼前动作。

4. 列车时刻表常用一般现在时：The service leaves at eleven. The train arrives at twelve ten. 说当前延误状态则可用 is running late。 The train is running late. 时刻表时间和眼前动作不同。

5. 拼写：wait → waiting；make → making（去不发音的 e）；sit → sitting（双写末尾辅音）。不要写 is wait、is makes 或 is siting。

6. know、need 等表示状态的动词在本课含义下用一般现在时：I know the platform. We need a valid ticket. 不写 I am knowing。luggage 是不可数名词：Our luggage is here，不能写 three luggages；可说 three bags 或 three pieces of luggage。

materials.title: A Journey with a Change of Plan
materials.passage:
Jade and Owen are meeting at the central railway terminal on Saturday morning. Their destination is a coastal town where a friend lives. The timetable lists a departure at 9:20 and an arrival at 10:10. They have chosen an express service because it makes fewer stops. The fare is higher than the fare for the slower service, but the shorter journey gives them more time with their friend.

Owen reaches the station first. He is pulling a small suitcase, while Jade is carrying their lunch. They keep their luggage close because the main hall is busy. A commuter beside them explains that she travels this way every weekday. Today she is visiting her sister instead of going to work. Each passenger needs a valid ticket before entering the platform area. Jade has a seat reservation in carriage three, but Owen has a ticket without a reserved seat.

At 9:05, they hear an announcement. There is a twenty-minute delay because workers are checking part of the track. The train will depart from platform six instead of platform four. Jade checks the display before they move. The change matters because another train is already waiting at platform four. It goes inland, in the opposite direction from their destination.

The friends discuss a connection through West Junction. That option would require a transfer, and the second train might leave before they reach it. They decide to stay with their direct service. Staff do not plan to cancel it; they expect the track check to finish soon. Jade sends their friend a message explaining that they will arrive later than planned. Their friend replies that she is meeting them outside the station and can wait.

When boarding begins, Owen asks the conductor whether he can sit beside Jade. The conductor checks the reservation display and finds an unreserved seat in the same carriage. He also points out the emergency information beside the door. They board carefully, put the suitcase in the luggage space and keep the aisle clear. Jade is reading the updated arrival time, while Owen is checking that they have all their bags.

The delay has changed their plan, but it has not ended their trip. They have checked the platform, chosen a workable route and told their friend what is happening. Before leaving home next time, they will check for travel updates as well as reading the printed timetable.

materials.title: Which Train Should We Take Now?
materials.transcript:
Jade: I'm at the ticket hall. Are you waiting on platform six?
Owen: No. The announcement has changed our platform to eight. I'm standing beside the stairs.
Jade: Is our express train still leaving at ten thirty?
Owen: It is running fifteen minutes late. The display now says ten forty-five.
Jade: Did the announcement explain the delay?
Owen: Yes. Staff are checking a signal beside the track near North Junction. They cannot say when it will be ready.
Jade: I don't want to cancel our journey, but we will miss our connection at North Junction. Shall we use a direct service instead?
Owen: Yes. The conductor says the eleven o'clock service goes directly to the coast. We won't need a transfer.
Jade: Is our ticket valid on that service?
Owen: Yes, but our seat reservation is not. We can ask for new seats at the desk.
Jade: I'd like a seat near the luggage space. This suitcase is heavy.
Owen: There are two seats together in carriage five. The fare is the same, so we don't need to pay extra.
Jade: Good. What is the new arrival time?
Owen: Twelve ten. I'll message our friend now. She is meeting us outside the station.
Jade: What if she gets there early?
Owen: The terminal has an indoor waiting room. She can wait there and come outside when our train arrives.
Jade: Thanks. I'm buying some water before we board. Do you want anything?
Owen: Just water. Please meet me by the stairs at ten fifty. We should allow ten minutes to get to the right carriage.
Jade: All right. I'll check the platform display again before I come.

materials.passage:
1. should / should not 表示建议或不建议，后面用动词原形，不随第三人称加 -s：She should bring the note. He should not guess the number. 这是交流安排的例句，不是诊疗建议。疑问句可将 should 提到主语前：Should I bring my card? 易错：不说 should brings，也不加 to。

materials.instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
materials.passage:
On Monday, Lena has an appointment at the Oak Street clinic at 10:15. She arrives early and goes to reception. A notice asks each patient to check that their name and phone number are correct. Lena notices that the last digit of her number is wrong, so she asks the receptionist to change it. The receptionist gives her a form and says that she can wait in the quiet room.

Lena has written one symptom on each line of a small card. Her list includes a cough and a sore throat. She also wants to mention a headache and pain in her shoulder. She has not measured her temperature today, and she does not know whether she has a fever. Rather than guessing, she leaves that part of the form empty. There is room for her to add a question about her stomach, too.

In the waiting room, Lena reads a poster about how to prepare for a conversation with a nurse. It suggests writing down an allergy and any previous injury if these are relevant. A visitor may also ask about a prescription or a treatment they do not understand. The poster asks visitors to bring the medicine label or a tablet package if they have a question. It suggests asking a professional what the word dose means on that label.

The poster shows a patient speaking with a nurse during an examination. In the picture, the patient asks what the word infection means. Lena also wants to understand the words people use in the clinic. She knows that a word on a poster is not a diagnosis. She can ask the clinic staff for advice about her own situation, and a pharmacy can answer questions about a label. She writes both questions down because she does not want to forget them.

Her friend David has agreed to meet her outside afterwards. He is visiting a dentist in another building, not the clinic. Lena sends him a short message: “My appointment is at 10:15. Please wait near the blue door.” David replies that he will bring a book while he waits. He remembers that Lena sometimes forgets her card when she is in a hurry.

Before her name is called, Lena looks at her list again. She adds questions about how to recover and when she might return to her usual routine. She has had less sleep than usual and wants to talk about a quiet afternoon of rest. She searches for words to describe feeling ill without saying that she already knows what is wrong. In the past, a walk in the park helped her feel healthy, and she wonders how to describe that. She plans to tell the nurse whether it is difficult to breathe while sitting quietly, then puts the card in her bag. Her plan is to describe what she notices and listen carefully rather than decide what the words mean for her health.

materials.transcript:
Mara: Is your appointment still on Thursday, Leo?
Leo: Yes, at two forty in the afternoon. I checked it this morning because I had written down two different times.
Mara: Where is the reception desk in that building?
Leo: It is beside the green entrance. The patient form is available there, and I can ask them to check the spelling of my name.
Mara: Have you prepared your questions?
Leo: I have a small list. I want to describe a cough, a sore throat and a headache. I will not guess a temperature or say I have a fever if I have not measured it.
Mara: Good. What about the pain you mentioned yesterday?
Leo: I will describe where it is and when I first noticed it. I also wrote down a question about my stomach. The nurse can ask for any other information during the examination.
Mara: Is there a place to ask about a prescription?
Leo: Yes. There is a pharmacy across the street. I have a question about a word on a medicine label, but I will ask the professional there rather than guess.
Mara: Which word is it?
Leo: Dose. I will show the tablet package and ask what the label means. I will not decide what to take from the word alone.
Mara: Did you write down your allergy question as well?
Leo: Yes. My main question is what information they need. I will ask the nurse how to describe how I breathe and when I might recover. I will also ask for advice about my treatment.
Mara: I can wait for you after my dentist visit.
Leo: Thanks. Please meet me by the yellow bench at three thirty, not at the green entrance. I will text you if the time changes.

materials.instructions: Read the passage and choose one answer for each question.
materials.passage:
Mina and her brother Ravi are shopping for a small neighborhood picnic. They have a budget of twenty-four pounds for food and drinks. Before leaving home, they write a list with a pound sign beside each price and agree that Ravi will check the prices while Mina carries a basket. They want enough food for six people, but they do not want to buy a large quantity that will go to waste.

At the first shelf, Mina finds a packet of beans for three pounds. They choose two packets, so the cost is six pounds. Nearby, a bag of rice has a price of four pounds. The label says that the bag contains one kilogram. Ravi also picks up carrots. A sign asks customers to weigh loose vegetables, and the scale shows a weight of one kilogram. The carrots cost four pounds.

The last item is one liter of oil for three pounds. Ravi checks the numbers on the list: six pounds for beans, four for rice, four for carrots and three for oil. The total before any reduction is seventeen pounds. Mina sees a package of paper plates, but it is expensive. There are plates at home, so they decide not to include that purchase. A cheap bag is not useful if they do not need it.

At the checkout, the assistant notices that the shop has agreed to discount their food by two pounds for a local event. The amount they need to pay is therefore fifteen pounds. Ravi plans to pay in cash with a twenty-pound note. The assistant gives him five one-pound coins as change and hands him a receipt. Mina counts every coin and checks the receipt before they leave.

Outside, the two discuss how much of the original budget remains. They spend fifteen pounds at the shop, leaving nine pounds for anything else the group decides to buy. They agree to save that money for now instead of choosing an unnecessary extra item. If the group later wants fruit, they can decide together what they can afford.

Ravi notices a poster for a similar picnic in the United States. Its example price is shown in dollars, and one small drink has a price of one dollar. The poster is not a currency exchange guide, so Mina does not compare it directly with a pound. They join a short queue to collect the picnic notice and walk home. Mina is pleased that the list and receipt explain their choices clearly.

materials.instructions: Listen to the two speakers and choose one answer. Use this dialogue rather than the reading passage.
materials.transcript:
Ella: We have a budget of twenty-five pounds for the soup evening. Have you made a list, Ben?
Ben: Yes. We need two loaves of bread, one bag of rice, three packets of soup and one liter of juice. Let us take a basket.
Ella: How much is the bread?
Ben: Each loaf has a price of two pounds fifty. Two loaves cost five pounds in total. The rice is six pounds for the bag.
Ella: The label says two kilograms, so we do not need to weigh it. The smaller one-kilogram bag was out of stock. What about the soup?
Ben: Each packet costs two pounds. The quantity is three, so that is six pounds. The juice is two pounds.
Ella: Then our total before the reduction is nineteen pounds. There is a card saying the shop will discount this purchase by three pounds.
Ben: That leaves an amount of sixteen pounds to pay. We can afford it and save nine pounds from our budget.
Ella: I have a twenty-pound note in cash. Will you check the change and receipt with me?
Ben: Of course. We should get four pounds back. If the assistant gives us a coin, we will count it with the notes.
Ella: Shall we take that package of cups too?
Ben: No. It is expensive, and the hall already has cups. A cheap extra is still unnecessary if we do not need it.
Ella: Agreed. In the shop near my old home, prices were shown in dollars. Here the pound sign is easy to see.
Ben: Let us join the queue and then take the food to the hall. We can tell the others exactly how much we spend.

materials.title: 比较级、同等比较与程度

questions.prompt: Compare the two rooms: the bedroom is smaller.

questions.explanation: too wide 指宽得超过空间所需，放不下。

questions.prompt: Choose the correct position of enough.

questions.explanation: 修饰形容词时 enough 放在形容词后。

options: The room is wide enough for the desk.

The room is too narrow for the desk.

answers: The room is wide enough for the desk.
questions.evidence: The room is wide enough for the desk.

materials.instructions: 阅读中文讲解及例句，再独立完成十二题并根据证据订正。
materials.passage:
1. 比较两者可用比较级 + than。短形容词常加 -er：The bedroom is smaller than the kitchen. The living room is bigger than the bedroom. big 末尾辅音双写；多音节词常用 more：Oak is more spacious than Elm. 不说 more bigger，也不要漏掉 than。

2. as + 形容词原级 + as 表示一样：Pine is as quiet as Cedar. not as + 原级 + as 表示前者不及后者：Pine is not as large as Cedar. 这里用 quiet、large 原级，而不是 quieter 或 larger。比较必须有明确的两个对象与比较维度。

3. too + 形容词表示超过所需程度：The desk is too wide for this room. 形容词 + enough 表示达到所需程度：The room is wide enough for the desk. enough 放在形容词后；名词前可说 enough space。too wide 不等于 wide enough，判断时要看句意。

materials.passage:
Lila and her cousin Ben want to move closer to their language class. They visit two places in the same neighborhood on Tuesday. The first apartment is on Oak Street, and the second is on Elm Street. Lila has written the address of each one in her notebook. She wants to compare the rooms and the monthly costs before making a decision.

The Oak apartment has a monthly rent of 720 pounds. Its bedroom is smaller than the one on Elm Street, but its kitchen is larger. The bathroom is private, and the living room feels spacious to both visitors. There is enough space for Ben's desk, and the window looks out onto a small garden. Lila likes the light, while Ben notices that the ceiling is higher than the ceiling in his current room.

The landlord says that the next tenant can use the furniture included in the apartment: a table, two chairs and a bed. Lila checks the floor beside the table and photographs a mark on the wall. She also sees a small leak near the bathroom door. The landlord says a repair is planned before the next tenant moves in. Lila writes this down and asks for the planned work to be included in their written agreement. She does not assume that a spoken promise is the same as completed work.

Ben asks how the heating works and whether electricity and gas are included. The landlord shows them an example bill and says the electricity charge is separate from the rent. The gas charge is also separate. Ben notes both points so that the family can ask about the likely costs later. They do not assume that rent covers every household expense.

The landlord shows Lila a draft contract for a twelve-month lease. The proposed deposit is 400 pounds. Lila wants to read the document carefully before signing and ask what happens if existing damage appears in the photographs. She and Ben take a copy home rather than agreeing at the door. The details in this fictional offer are specific to this apartment.

The Elm apartment costs 760 pounds each month. It is as quiet as the Oak apartment, but the kitchen is not as large. Its gate looks secure, although Lila knows that a quick look cannot guarantee safety. On the bus home, Ben says that Oak is better for his desk but that the leak and the separate bills need answers. Lila agrees. They will compare the notes, ask their questions and then decide together.

materials.passage:
1. 描述已结束的过去事件用一般过去时。规则动词通常加 -ed：Maya visited the center. 不规则形式需记忆：She wrote an application. They went to the interview. 时间线索如 yesterday 或 last week 有助判断，但动词也必须变为正确过去式；不说 she writed。

2. 过去时否定用 did not + 动词原形：She did not arrive late. 一般疑问句用 Did + 主语 + 动词原形：Did Maya meet the manager? 简短回答 Yes, she did. did 已承担过去时，不再把后面的动词写成过去式；不说 Did Maya met 或 did not arrived。

3. because 引出原因，so 引出结果：Maya practiced because the interview was important. The room was quiet, so she spoke clearly. 两个句子先找原因再找结果；一个基本句中不要重复使用 because ... so。because 和 so 所连接内容必须符合句意，不能只按位置猜测。

materials.passage:
On Monday, Maya saw a vacancy for a part-time visitor-desk position at a community center. She wanted to learn about the role before sending an application. The notice said that the employee would help visitors find rooms and answer simple questions. Maya liked the idea because she had enjoyed helping people at a library.

Maya spoke to her former colleague, Lina, about her experience. At the library, they had worked as a team during a busy reading event. Maya explained that her strongest skill was listening carefully when someone asked for help. Lina remembered that Maya was reliable: she arrived on time and checked her work before leaving. This gave Maya a useful example to describe to the employer.

On Tuesday, Maya completed the application and listed a certificate from a basic computer course. The notice mentioned the course as a useful qualification, but it did not say that the certificate was required. Maya did not claim to have a qualification she had not earned. She wanted an opportunity to learn more, and her longer-term career goal was to work in community education.

The next morning, the center invited her to an interview with the manager of its visitor department. Maya brought the notice and a copy of her application. The manager asked each candidate to explain how they would respond if a customer could not find a room. Maya said she would listen, check the room list and ask a colleague when she was unsure. She also asked which task a new worker would learn first.

During the conversation, the manager described the service and explained one responsibility: helping people find accurate information. The visitor desk was run with support from a local company, whose main business was organizing community events. The manager said the part-time role paid an hourly wage of twelve pounds. A monthly salary appeared in a separate notice for a different, full-time role. Maya wrote down the difference and planned to ask about working hours before making any decision.

Maya did not receive a job offer at the interview. The manager said the center would contact candidates the following week. Maya felt successful in explaining her own example clearly, even though she did not yet know the result. On Thursday she planned to resume her library volunteering. Here resume means begin again; it is a verb, not the name of a job document. The profession interested her, so she kept the notes and thought about what she wanted to improve for the next conversation.

Jo: How was your interview at the neighborhood museum on Friday, Rina?
Rina: It was interesting. I went at eleven in the morning and spoke to the manager of the events department.
Jo: What position did you apply for?
Rina: The vacancy was for a weekend workshop assistant. I sent the application on Wednesday. The employer wanted someone to help visitors find materials.
Jo: Did you give an example of your experience?
Rina: Yes. I described a garden event where my colleague and I worked as a team. I showed a certificate from a short art course as one qualification. I also brought a copy of my application for the manager.
Jo: What did they ask about?
Rina: They asked how I would help a customer who arrived late. I said I would listen, check the task list and ask an employee if I was unsure.
Jo: Did they explain the pay?
Rina: Yes. The hourly wage was fourteen pounds. The manager also mentioned a monthly salary, but that was for a different full-time position.
Jo: Did you get a decision at the interview?
Rina: No. They will contact each candidate next Tuesday. My goal was to speak clearly, and I felt successful in giving my example.
Jo: What will you do while you wait?
Rina: I will resume my library volunteering on Sunday. I enjoy that service, and I want to build a reliable work routine for my career.
Jo: Did you ask about the first responsibility?
Rina: Yes. A new assistant starts by preparing tables before visitors arrive. I wrote it in my notes, because this opportunity could teach me a new skill.

materials.passage:
Mia helps at a neighborhood garden. On Sunday, she and other volunteers plan to show children how to plant seeds. The weather may change, so Mia reads the forecast on Friday. It says the morning will be cloudy, but there may be sunshine after lunch. The temperature is likely to reach 14 degrees Celsius. Because the weather may change, Mia asks the team to prepare both an outside table and a room inside the community center.

Last year the same event was sunny, and the children worked outside all day. This year a dark cloud has appeared over the hills earlier than expected. Mia thinks the rain is going to start soon, so she moves the paper instructions indoors. A strong wind could blow the papers away even if the ground stays dry. Each child will need an umbrella if they walk between the room and the garden during rain.

The center has a simple rule for a storm: everyone goes inside when they hear thunder or see lightning. The group will wait in the room until staff say it is safe to return. The indoor activity uses small pots, soil and seeds, so the children can still take a plant home. Mia checks that the room has enough chairs and a place to wash hands.

A local gardener offers to explain why conditions differ through the year. In spring, the town is usually mild and the soil becomes warm enough for seeds. Summer can be hot, so the garden team waters plants early. In autumn, a windy day may bring leaves onto the paths. Winter is the cold season; a snowy morning is exciting for children, but snow can cover the small plants. On a freezing night, volunteers sometimes move young plants into a sheltered room.

The gardener also reminds Mia that climate describes patterns over many years, while a forecast describes expected conditions at a particular time. A rainy week does not explain the whole climate of the town. Fog sometimes makes the road hard to see, and high humidity can make a warm room feel uncomfortable. These details help the team decide when to open windows and when to offer an indoor space.

On Sunday morning, Mia will check the new report before the families arrive. If the sky stays safe, the children will plant outside. If conditions change, they will use the room instead. The activity has a clear purpose in either place: each child can learn how to care for a seed.

options: I have played tennis. I have played it last year.

answers: I have played tennis. I played it last year.

materials.instructions: 先阅读说明与例句，再作答并根据解释订正。
materials.passage:
1. 现在完成时可谈到目前为止的经历，不说具体已结束的时间：I have played tennis. She has tried yoga. 结构是 have / has + 过去分词；he / she / it 用 has。一般疑问句把 have / has 提到主语前：Have you ever played tennis? 肯定回答 Yes, I have. 不用 did。

2. ever 常用于问“曾经”；never 表示从未，本身已有否定意义：I have never played volleyball. 不再加 not。already 常放在 have / has 后：He has already tried basketball. yet 常放在否定句或疑问句末：She has not decided yet. Has Sol decided yet? 这些词的位置有常见用法，但也有其他表达方式。

3. 过去具体结束的时间用一般过去时：We borrowed rackets last year. 不写 We have borrowed rackets last year。经历问题可以先问 Have you ever played tennis? 再用 I played tennis last year. 提供已结束时间。I have played tennis. I played it last year.注意过去分词：go → gone、do → done 是不规则形式；play → played 是规则形式。

4. been 与 gone 的含义不同：She has been to the gym. 表示她去过并已回来；She has gone to the gym. 通常表示她去了，现在仍在那儿或途中。谈过去经历时，不要把 have gone 一律当作 have been。

materials.instructions: Read the passage and choose ONE answer for each question.
materials.passage:
Ines wants a hobby that gives her time with other people. She has worked from home for several months, and most of her leisure time has been quiet. A community center is offering a Saturday activity day, so she asks her friend Sol to go with her. Neither of them wants to choose a sport only because it is popular. They hope to find exercise that feels enjoyable enough to continue.

At the center, a fitness coach explains that beginners can try short sessions before joining a class. Ines has never played tennis, but she has already watched a tennis match on television. She borrows a racket and practices hitting a ball over a low net. Sol tries basketball nearby and finds that passing to a partner is harder than it looks. They both laugh when the ball goes in the wrong direction.

The center also has a volleyball group, and a teacher invites visitors to join a simple practice. Ines likes the way teammates call to one another. Sol, however, prefers the music in an aerobics class. She says she has not decided which activity to join yet. They agree to come back the following week before paying for a whole term.

Outside, a volunteer explains that people can cycle on a marked path or jog around the park. Those who prefer to hike can join a walking group that leaves from the gym. The center lends a helmet to anyone using one of its bicycles. For a quieter choice, yoga is offered in a small room after lunch. The equipment for each session is included in the cost of the day.

In the afternoon, the friends visit the stadium to watch a local competition. One young athlete tells them that the goal is to learn from every match. Her team can win or lose, but they always thank their opponent. In the first game, the score is four to two. The winner of that game does not become the champion immediately; each team still has another game to play.

One spectator asks whether the stronger team will defeat every visiting team. The athlete says nobody knows until the games are played. Ines appreciates that answer. She and Sol leave before the final game because they have promised to cook dinner together. On the way home, Ines chooses the volleyball practice as her next step, while Sol plans to return to aerobics. They have discovered different interests without needing to be experts.

materials.instructions: Listen to the two speakers and choose ONE answer for each question. The facts differ from the reading.
materials.transcript:
Liam: Have you chosen an activity for the leisure club day next month?
Rosa: Not yet. I want a hobby I can share with my brother, but our fitness levels are different. He is a keen athlete, and I have only recently started to exercise.
Liam: Have you ever played tennis together?
Rosa: Yes, we have. We borrowed a racket each from the center last year, and I enjoyed it. He wants to try a different sport this time.
Liam: The gym has a beginner volleyball session at ten. Its coach says no experience is needed, and the equipment is included.
Rosa: That sounds good. My brother has already tried basketball, but I have never played volleyball. We could learn together.
Liam: There is also an aerobics class at twelve, followed by yoga at two. Both are indoors, so the weather will not matter.
Rosa: I enjoy music, but my brother prefers a game with a ball. Let's book the ten o'clock session. How much does it cost?
Liam: Six dollars for each person. The center asks visitors to book by Thursday, because the room is small.
Rosa: I will tell him tonight. Could we cycle there? He has a bicycle, and I can borrow one.
Liam: Yes, and please wear a helmet. You can leave the bikes next to the front door. There is also a place to jog or hike in the park afterward.
Rosa: Is there a competition at the stadium that day too? I would like to watch a match after our session.
Liam: Yes. The first game begins at four. You can be a spectator without paying, and the coach will explain the score.
Rosa: Great. I do not mind who will win or lose. It will be fun to see how each opponent works with their team.
Liam: The winner gets a small cup, but nobody has to be a champion to join the morning sessions.

materials.passage:
Marta wants to help her neighborhood club share its meeting notes. She knows that technology can make the work easier, but she has never used the club's shared website. On Tuesday she visits a digital help desk at the community center. The volunteer, Leo, lets her practice on a device that the center keeps for lessons. It uses a practice account with no real members' details.

Leo first shows Marta the hardware. The keyboard is used for typing, while the mouse moves the pointer on the screen. He asks her to open the browser and connect to the center's wireless network. Once the device has internet access, Marta can open the club's practice website. Leo explains that the website has an online area for shared notes and an offline guide saved on the computer.

At the login screen, Marta enters the practice username and password. Leo tells her not to share a real password with other people. If someone forgets a real password, the club asks that person to contact its administrator. Leo adds that no one should send a real password in an email. This rule keeps private details out of a message that could be read by the wrong person.

Marta opens a folder called Meetings and finds a file from a practice event. First she opens the document and adds the next meeting date. Then she saves a copy on the device. Before she closes it, she checks that the date and place are correct. After that, she uses the button to upload her copy to the shared area. Leo points out the new file name so she can confirm that the right version is there.

Next, Marta learns how to download a blank notes form for the next meeting. She wants to use it at home, where she can write without a connection. If the connection is unavailable, the local form still opens. Later she can connect again and share the finished notes with club members. She understands that a local copy and a shared copy are stored in different places.

The center also explains that software sometimes needs attention. Volunteers update the practice program before lessons, and they install new tools only when the center approves them. Marta need not make those changes herself. When she finishes, she uses the logout button and closes the browser. At the next club meeting she plans to ask the members who should be allowed to read the notes.

materials.transcript:
Omar: The club meeting is on Friday. Can we prepare a digital document with the agenda today?
June: Yes. First, let's connect the laptop to the wireless network. The internet is working, and I can open the club website in the browser.
Omar: Is this our real account? I do not want to use my usual password during a lesson.
June: No, this is a practice account. The username is printed on the lesson card, and the password is on a separate card. We will remove both cards after practice.
Omar: I can type with the keyboard, but the mouse is not moving the pointer. Is that a hardware problem?
June: Maybe. Press this small button underneath it first. If the mouse is switched off, the pointer does not move. There, it works now.
Omar: Good. After the login screen, I see a folder called Events. Which file should I open?
June: Open the one called Agenda Practice. Then add Friday's start time, which is six thirty. Before you save it, check that the room is number twelve.
Omar: Done. I will save a copy on the device. Should I upload it to the shared area now?
June: Yes, but use the practice area, not the real members' area. After you upload it, check that its name appears on the page.
Omar: I can see it. Can I download the blank form as well? I want offline access when I am traveling without a connection.
June: Of course. You do not need to install any new software for this form. The center staff update the program when necessary.
Omar: Should I send an email to the club today?
June: Wait until we check the real agenda tomorrow. For now, use the logout button before leaving the computer. Online notes can be useful, but we need to check them carefully.
Omar: Thanks. This technology is less confusing when we take one step at a time.

materials.instructions: Read the passage and choose ONE answer for each question.
materials.passage:
Lena wants to return to education after several years away from study. She works during the day, so she visits a local college to ask about an evening course. A friendly adviser explains that visitors can attend one sample lesson before they choose. Lena does not need a degree to join the introductory classes, and she can study one subject at a time.

The adviser gives her a map of the campus and invites her to a lecture about learning as an adult. After the talk, a graduate describes how she managed her time while working. She enjoyed reading on the bus and decided to keep one evening free for family. Lena likes the practical advice because she also needs a realistic weekly plan.

In the next room, people in a small seminar are discussing how a town changes over time. Participants compare old photographs, share questions and take notes. The teacher offers a tutorial for anyone who wants individual help after the group discussion. Lena learns that a seminar usually asks students to contribute, while a lecture often gives more time to the speaker.

A science teacher shows visitors a safe experiment with water and light in a supervised laboratory. She explains that biology, chemistry and physics can each ask different questions about the world. In the sample activity, students write a short report to describe what they observe. They do not need to know the answer before they begin; careful notes matter more than a quick guess.

Another classroom is displaying projects that connect history and geography. One pupil from a nearby school has drawn a map showing how a street looked in the past. The display also includes a literature project in which students write about a place in a story. Lena thinks the different subjects could help her understand her own neighborhood.

At the advice desk, she asks about homework and assessment. The adviser says that one assignment asks students to do simple research and write an essay. A teacher gives comments on the first draft before the final version is handed in. The curriculum also includes basic algebra for students who want to work with numbers. Lena is relieved to learn that help is available if a topic feels difficult.

Lena plans to take the local evening class first. If she enjoys it, she may later apply to a university, but today she wants to make one manageable decision. She writes the class time in her calendar and takes the teacher's contact details. Her aim is not to finish quickly; it is to build a study habit she can maintain.

materials.instructions: 先阅读说明与例句，再作答并根据解释订正。
materials.passage:
1. 一般现在时被动语态用 am / is / are + 过去分词，表示动作承受者：Plastic bottles are placed in a box. 单数用 is：A sign is displayed on the wall. 否定在 be 后加 not，如 The cans are not placed here. 不要漏 be，也不要把复数 bottles 搭配 is。

2. 需要指出执行者时用 by + 执行者：Rubbish is collected by volunteers. 当读者需要知道是谁做的，可保留 by volunteers；执行者未知或不重要时，可以省略：Rubbish is collected. by 后是执行者，不是动作承受者。

3. 描述过程时，根据重点选择主动或被动：Volunteers sort the bottles. 强调执行者；The bottles are sorted. 强调处理对象。两句均为一般现在时。过程可以写 First, the bottles are sorted. Then they are collected. 注意不规则过去分词 write → written；动词过去式与过去分词并非总是相同。

During the walk, the guide points to a tree where birds are resting. The river provides water and food for different kinds of wildlife. A quiet section of the bank is a habitat for one species of small bird. To protect the birds, visitors are asked to stay on the path. The guide explains that noise and litter can harm animals, even when people do not intend to cause a problem.

At the display, a large map shows how the river passes a lake before it eventually reaches the ocean. Another picture shows a forest on higher ground. The guide uses these examples to introduce ecology, the study of relationships among living things and their surroundings. She explains that conservation starts with noticing what a place needs. The class does not claim that one action can solve all pollution; it considers several small, practical choices.

In a covered area, volunteers show how they sort waste from community events. Clean plastic bottles are placed in one box, and metal cans are placed in another. The town's program accepts these materials so local workers can recycle them. Volunteers also reuse pieces of wood to make signs, so useful material does not have to be thrown away. They reduce waste by offering a water refill point instead of handing out single-use bottles.

A visitor asks why one sign says rubbish and another says garbage. The organizer explains that both words can mean unwanted material, and different English speakers may prefer one or the other. A second sign reminds visitors not to leave food wrappers on the ground. At the end of the day, rubbish from the walk is collected by volunteers and taken to the correct bins.

Inside the hall, a model shows how sunlight can provide renewable energy for a small lamp. The organizer calls the model an example of a natural source of power. The group discusses what a sustainable event might involve: using resources carefully and considering future needs. Families write one idea on a card, such as bringing a reusable bottle or helping keep the path clean.

The cards are displayed on a board after the event. The organizer plans to read them before arranging the next community day. She hopes the ideas will lead to actions that neighbors can continue throughout the year.

Sara: Are you ready for our school's environment event next week?
Jon: Almost. It is on Thursday at two, and the hall is booked. I want visitors to understand how we can reduce waste at school.
Sara: I have made a sign about litter near the river. After lunch, paper and plastic are often left beside the path. We need to protect the wildlife there.
Jon: Good. We should explain that litter can harm a bird's habitat. I will ask the nature club to show a picture of one local species.
Sara: Shall we call the activity a cleanup? I have gloves for twelve students, and the rubbish will be collected in bags.
Jon: Yes, but first we will check the path with a teacher. The cleanup will start at three, after the hall discussion.
Sara: I also have a box for clean metal cans. In our school's program, those cans are accepted for recycling. Can we recycle plastic there too?
Jon: Only the bottles listed on the school notice. We should read the notice before we put anything in the box. Other garbage goes in the regular bin.
Sara: What about the old wood from the garden signs? Could we reuse it instead of buying new material?
Jon: Yes. It is kept in the storage room, and the art group will turn it into new signs. That is one sustainable choice we can explain.
Sara: I want to add a display about renewable energy. The science class has a small model that uses sunlight to power a lamp.
Jon: Bring it, please. We can put it beside the map of the lake and the ocean. The geography teacher is drawing arrows to show where the water goes.
Sara: I will make a second card about ecology and conservation, too. It can ask visitors how their choices affect a natural place.
Jon: Great. After the event, the ideas are read by the club, and we choose one to try the following month.

Sara and Ben are new students at an English class. At ten, they meet their teacher, Ms Lee. There is a group of six students. Sara and Ben are two of the six. Ms Lee says hello and shows them the room. The students can ask for help. There are two tables in the room. The group can sit at the tables. They have time to learn together. Ms Lee is happy to help the new students.

Three textbooks are on one table. Four notebooks are on another table. Sara has a notebook. Ben has one too. Ms Lee has a marker. She writes her name on the board. She says, "This is my name. Please write your name in your notebook."

Sara and Ben sit at a table. Ms Lee says, "Please open your textbook." The group can read a short note together. The note has five names. Sara reads one name. Ben reads another. They do not need to read very fast. The teacher can help them.

Ben has a question about a sound. He says, "I do not understand this sound. Please speak again." Ms Lee says the sound again. Ben tries it. He wants to check his answer. He asks, "How do you spell this name?" Ms Lee shows him the letters.

The students stand and speak to one another. Sara says, "I am fine. Thank you, Ms Lee." Ben says, "Thank you for your help." They write one more note and show it to the teacher. The group is small, and everyone has time to ask a question.

materials.transcript:
Ava: Hello. My name is Ava. We meet our English group at six. There are four students in this group. What is your name?

Tom: My name is Tom. I am a new student too. Three textbooks are on that table. Two notebooks are on this table. The teacher has a marker.

Ava: Please sit here, Tom. This is my notebook. Is that your textbook? We can open our books and write our names. I can show you my note.

Tom: Yes, this is my textbook. I have a question. I do not understand one sound. Can you speak again, please? I want to check the sound before I read.

Ava: Yes. Listen to the sound. I can help you spell the name. The name is Ben. It has three letters. We can say the letters together.

Tom: Thank you, Ava. I can spell Ben now. I write the name in my notebook. I ask the teacher to check my work.

Ava: Yes. The teacher can help us. We have ten minutes for a short task. Please read the note and then stand near the group. We can speak to the other students. The teacher shows us the next part. We can listen together. It is fine to ask for help.

Tom: Thank you. I have five names on my note, but I read only one name first. Then we can ask the teacher another question.

questions.prompt: Use the simple present: I ____ at ten.
questions.evidence: I start at ten.
questions.explanation: I 后的一般现在时用原形 start；starts 用于 he/she，starting 单独使用缺助动词，started 是过去式。

questions.prompt: Use the simple present: She ____ at ten.
questions.evidence: She starts at ten.
questions.explanation: 一般现在时 she 后用 starts；start 不合此处主谓搭配，starting 单独使用缺助动词，started 是过去式。

questions.prompt: Use the simple present: I ____ at four.
questions.evidence: I finish at four.
questions.explanation: I 后的一般现在时用原形 finish；finishes 用于 he/she，finishing 单独使用缺助动词，finished 是过去式。

questions.prompt: Use the simple present: He ____ at four.
questions.evidence: He finishes at four.
questions.explanation: 一般现在时 he 后用 finishes；finish 不合此处主谓搭配，finishing 单独使用缺助动词，finished 是过去式。

questions.prompt: Complete the negative: I ____ not leave at six.
questions.evidence: I do not leave at six.
questions.explanation: 主语 I 的一般现在时否定用 do not；does 用于 he/she，am 和 is 不能替代这里的 do。

questions.prompt: Complete the negative: She ____ not leave at six.
questions.evidence: She does not leave at six.
questions.explanation: 主语 she 的一般现在时否定用 does not；do、are 和 is 不能构成这个结构。

questions.prompt: Complete the negative: I do not ____ at five.
questions.evidence: I do not start at five.
questions.explanation: do not 后用动词原形 start；starts、starting 和 started 不能直接用在这里。

questions.prompt: Complete the negative: He does not ____ at five.
questions.evidence: He does not start at five.
questions.explanation: does not 后仍用原形 start，不能再加 -s；其他形式也不符合这个否定句。

questions.prompt: Complete the question: ____ you read this note every day?
questions.evidence: 询问习惯时，Do 放在 I / you 前，Does 放在 he / she 前；后面用动词原形。简短回答与提问中的 do / does 一致。
questions.explanation: 询问 you 的动作习惯用 Do；Does 对应 he/she，Is 和 Are 不构成这个动作问句。

questions.prompt: Complete the question: ____ he put on a shirt every morning?
questions.evidence: 询问习惯时，Do 放在 I / you 前，Does 放在 he / she 前；后面用动词原形。简短回答与提问中的 do / does 一致。
questions.explanation: 询问 he 的动作习惯用 Does，后面 put 保持原形；Do、Is 和 Are 不符合这个结构。

questions.prompt: Answer the question: Does she leave at ten every day? Yes, she ____.
questions.evidence: 询问习惯时，Do 放在 I / you 前，Does 放在 he / she 前；后面用动词原形。简短回答与提问中的 do / does 一致。
questions.explanation: Does she 开头的肯定简答用 Yes, she does；do、is 和 are 与该问句不对应。

questions.prompt: Answer the question: Do you stay here on class days? No, I ____ not.
questions.evidence: 询问习惯时，Do 放在 I / you 前，Does 放在 he / she 前；后面用动词原形。简短回答与提问中的 do / does 一致。
questions.explanation: Do you 问句的否定简答为 No, I do not；does 用于 he/she，am 和 is 不对应这里的动作问句。

materials.instructions: 先读中文解释和例句，做前 8 道引导题，再做 4 道新情境题；不确定时可回看规则。
materials.passage:
1. 一般现在时描述习惯。I 和 you 后通常用动词原形；he 和 she 表示一个人时，动词通常加 -s，部分词加 -es。先找主语再选动词。
例句：I start at ten. She starts at ten. I finish at four. He finishes at four.

2. 否定习惯时，I / you 后用 do not 加动词原形；he / she 后用 does not 加动词原形。does 已表示第三人称，后面的动词不再加 -s。
例句：I do not leave at six. She does not leave at six. I do not start at five. He does not start at five.

3. 询问习惯时，Do 放在 I / you 前，Does 放在 he / she 前；后面用动词原形。简短回答与提问中的 do / does 一致。
例句：Do you eat lunch? Does she eat lunch?

My name is Hana. Today I have an English class. On class days, I wake at six. I get up. My bed is near the chair. The room is cool. I wash my face and look at my hair. My shirt is on a chair. A dress is on the chair too. I choose the shirt today. The dress is for tomorrow.

I put a sock on each foot. Then I put on one shoe and the other. The sun is out. I put a hat on my head before I leave. At the door, I lift my hand and wave to my friend Leo. A short walk helps my body feel ready for class.

I take a quick look at the time. I take a slow walk to class. I start class at ten. Leo starts at ten too. He wakes at five, but I wake at six. We meet our group at the table. We open our books and say hello to the teacher. I do not need to hurry.

I eat lunch at one. After lunch, I read a short note. I finish class at four. Leo finishes at four too. I stay in the room for five minutes to check my note. Then I leave. Leo has a question for the teacher, so he stays for a short time too.

I eat dinner at six. Before dinner, I write a note for tomorrow. It has my class time and one question. This is my plan for a class day. Leo has a different plan. We can change our plans when we need to.

questions.explanation: 结合“下课后留下五分钟”和紧接着“检查给老师的便条”两句，可推断她留下是为了检查便条；没有说留下吃晚饭、等到十点或找鞋。

questions.prompt: What does Cal do after class?
options: He takes a quick walk to the shop.
He puts his shoe under the bed.
He takes a slow walk to the shop.
He starts another class at ten.
answers: He takes a slow walk to the shop.
questions.evidence: Then I leave with you. I take a slow walk to the shop.
questions.explanation: Cal 随 Nia 离开并慢慢走去商店；他没有说快走、把鞋放床下或十点再开始一节课。

questions.prompt: When does Nia eat dinner?
questions.evidence: I eat dinner at six.
questions.explanation: Nia 六点吃晚饭；一点吃午饭，三点下课，五点起床。

questions.prompt: Which item does Nia say she plans to wear tomorrow?
questions.evidence: I plan to wear my dress tomorrow.
questions.explanation: Nia 说计划明天穿连衣裙；蓝衬衫和帽子是她今天使用的物品，Cal 的衬衫也不是她说的明日计划。

materials.instructions: 先按对话分段听人物与数字，再独立作答；订正时回听对应片段。
materials.transcript:
Nia: Hello, Cal. On class days, I wake at five. I get up and wash my face. My room is cool. What time do you wake?

Cal: I wake at six. I put on a shirt. I put a sock on each foot. My shoe is under the bed. I find it and put it on.

Nia: I have a blue shirt today. I also have a dress, but I choose the shirt. The sun is out, so I put a hat on my head before I leave.

Cal: I take a quick look at my note. I start class at ten. Do you start at ten too? We can meet our group at the table.

Nia: Yes. I start at ten. I eat lunch at one and finish class at three. After class, I stay in the room for five minutes. I check a note for the teacher.

Cal: I finish at three too. Then I leave with you. I take a slow walk to the shop. A short walk helps my body feel ready for the next part of the day.

Nia: I lift my hand to wave to a friend. I eat dinner at six. Before dinner, I write my class time for tomorrow. I plan to wear my dress tomorrow.

Cal: That is a good plan. I check my hair before dinner. I do not need the same plan as you. We can each choose our own times.
